entries.title: Psalms 45:1
segments: The theme of this psalm is Jesus Christ the King of kings, and the espousal of his church to him.  In the Old Testament, God is often represented as the husband of Zion, that is, of his church.
.  In like manner the New Testament church is called "the bride, the Lamb's wife," and she is "arrayed in fine linen, clean and white," for the day of her marriage.

The espousal of the Saviour to his church is here represented under imagery borrowed from the marriage customs of eastern nations. 
 
  Inditing; meditating in preparation to speak. 
 
  The king; Jesus Christ. 
 
  The pen of a ready writer; the fulness of his feelings makes his tongue fervent and rapid in its utterance, like the pen of a ready writer. 
 
The thoughts of true believers are very much occupied about Christ and his cause.

entries.title: Psalms 45:2
segments: Grace is poured into thy lips; he received the Holy Spirit without measure.

entries.title: Psalms 45:3
segments: Since God has given to Christ all power in heaven and in earth, and made him "most mighty" in behalf of the church, they who love the prosperity of his kingdom shall see their utmost desires fulfilled.

entries.title: Psalms 45:5
segments: The king's enemies; the enemies of Christ.  Compare

entries.title: Psalms 45:6
segments: O God; this is applied by the Holy Spirit to Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ is God over all; he is so addressed by the Father, and his works prove him to be divine.

entries.title: Psalms 45:8
segments: Myrrh, and aloes, and cassia; put for sweet odors generally.  The aloes here spoken of are the lign-aloes, mentioned
.  It is a species of fragrant wood.

entries.title: Psalms 45:9
segments: Gold Ophir; Ophir is here mentioned as emphatically the gold-land of the ancient Hebrews.  For its situation see note to

entries.title: Psalms 45:10
segments:
Forget--thine own people; be wholly devoted to Jesus Christ, and love him more than father, mother, or any earthly friend. 
 
Those who would partake of Christ's salvation must love him supremely, and be ready, when called, to forsake all for his sake.

entries.title: Psalms 45:11
segments: Thy beauty; the holiness and spiritual beauty of his church.

entries.title: Psalms 45:12
segments: The daughter of Tyre; that is, Tyre herself, represented as a princely female.  The Tyrians were celebrated for their extensive commerce and great wealth.  The general idea is, that the rich and mighty should contribute their offerings to Christ and his bride the church.

entries.title: Psalms 45:13
segments:
The king's daughter; Christ's redeemed and sanctified church. 
 
  Within; within the king's palace.  Her glorious apparel represents her spiritual beauty. 
 
Divine grace changes the heart and makes it meet to be a habitation for God through his Spirit.

entries.title: Psalms 45:16
segments:
Thy children; the children of the King: the church of Christ is here, as elsewhere, represented as the mother of a numerous and honorable offspring. 
 
Death is continually removing the fathers from Christ's church; but the number and strength of Christ's spiritual offspring on earth shall be increased, till they shall inherit the world.  In that happy day the righteous shall be "princes in all the earth."
